findings.title: Finding closure is taken from orchestrator-written findings.json; the reviewer's own verification sidecar, the verification evidence and the fix revision are never checked
findings.reproduction: tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs:408-418 accepts CLOSED_VERIFIED/REJECTED_INVALID when findings.json carries a verification object with result PASS, by_role != owner and a valid run. collectRaisedFindings (rules.mjs:342-367; filename filter at :360) never reads <role>.verifications.json, so the reviewer-authored verification is not the source of truth. verification.evidence paths and fix_revision (rules.mjs:416 only checks truthiness) are not checked. Reproduced with GATE_TOOLS=/tmp/dg0-sec-r2 node --test docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/code-security/round-2/repro-r2.test.mjs: (N1b) on a fully valid gate, add round-2/code-security-reviewer.verifications.json {finding_id F-DG0-101, result FAIL, status_after OPEN} while findings.json says CLOSED_VERIFIED/PASS citing that reviewer's round-2 run. validateGate returns []. (N1c) Set fix_revision 'not-a-commit' and verification.evidence ['does/not/exist.log']. validateGate returns []. Precondition: whoever maintains findings.json (the orchestrator, D-008) writes the verification object directly instead of via import-findings.mjs. The reporter's final-round record can still be PASS, because nothing ties a PASS verdict to the absence of a FAIL verification.
findings.expected: A finding reaches CLOSED_VERIFIED/REJECTED_INVALID only if a reviewer-authored verifications sidecar in a round of this stage contains an entry for that finding with result PASS and a matching status_after. The sidecar belongs to a PASS or FAIL record whose run is bound (assignment and post-freeze, as for reviews). findings.json.verification must equal that entry. Verification evidence must be existing repository files, and fix_revision must be a commit that is an ancestor of the candidate's source_commit. A FAIL entry in a later round supersedes an earlier PASS.
findings.actual: The gate's 'zero unresolved Critical/High and mandatory findings' condition can be met by editing one object in findings.json, even when the reporting reviewer explicitly recorded the fix as FAIL.

findings.title: Write guard: an implementer can plant a nested '.git' (tools/.git, docs/.git, .github/.git) that moves the guard's repo root and un-protects gate rules, sources and delivery records
findings.reproduction: tools/agents/guard-write.mjs:40-48 (repoRootOf) takes the nearest ancestor containing '.git' as the repository root, and :72 matches patterns against the path relative to that root. solution-architect/frontend/backend/kpi/devops have allow '**'. 'tools/.git', 'docs/.git' and '.github/.git' match no deny pattern, so a Write to them is allowed. After Write tools/.git ('gitdir: /nonexistent'), a Write to tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs is evaluated as 'gates/lib/rules.mjs' and ALLOWED. The same holds for tools/agents/write-scopes.json (via tools/.git), docs/delivery/stages.json and docs/source/playbook.md (via docs/.git), and .github/workflows/delivery-gates.yml (via .github/.git). Reproduced through decide() and end-to-end through the hook entry point (exit 0): repro-r2 test N3. The planted file is invisible in 'git status' (09-nested-git-visibility.log), so it persists silently for later sessions. Edits to tracked protected files still show as ' M' and change the candidate, so the orchestrator's git-status check and the candidate hash remain compensating controls. Bash remains unguarded (disclosed, D-009/D-020); this finding is about the Write-tool guard itself.
findings.expected: The guard uses a fixed repository root (for example the root of the tree containing tools/agents/guard-write.mjs, or `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` evaluated once by the hook) rather than the nearest '.git'. It also denies writes of any path segment named '.git' (the pattern '**/.git' and '**/.git/**') for every role.
findings.actual: Implementer roles can disable the write guard for protected paths with two Write calls, and the first one leaves no trace in git status.

findings.title: Candidate identity omits the entry type and the file mode: a file containing 'symlink:<t>' collides with a symlink to <t>, and chmod +x/-x does not change the candidate
findings.reproduction: tools/gates/lib/candidate.mjs:58-60 hashes a symlink as sha256('symlink:'+target). candidateId (:117-124) serialises only '<sha256>  <path>', dropping entry.type, so a regular file whose bytes are 'symlink:app.txt' hashes identically to a symlink -> app.txt (repro-r2 N4). The git mode (100644 vs 100755) is not hashed either, so removing the executable bit from tools/source/check_extraction.sh (which CI runs directly) or tools/agents/run-agent.sh leaves the candidate unchanged (repro-r2 N5).
findings.expected: The canonical line includes the type and the mode, e.g. '<sha256>  <mode>  <path>', with mode taken from git (100644/100755/120000) in both manifestFromRef and manifestFromWorkingTree.
findings.actual: Two distinct deliverables share one candidate ID; a behaviour-changing mode change is invisible to A25 change detection. Exploitation of the collision requires crafting a file whose content equals the link's marker string; impact is low. I would accept this as a Low observation.

findings.title: Working-tree candidate depends on the platform's line-ending conversion; no .gitattributes pins it
findings.reproduction: manifestFromWorkingTree (tools/gates/lib/candidate.mjs:73-96) hashes on-disk bytes, while manifestFromRef hashes blobs. With core.autocrlf=true (the Git for Windows default), checked-out text files contain CRLF, so candidate.mjs --stage and validate.mjs --stage (current mode) compute a different ID from the frozen one (repro-r2 N6). The repository has no .gitattributes, and D-005 is silent on line endings. The effect is fail-closed (a false 'changed' result, not a bypass).
findings.expected: Either a committed .gitattributes ('* -text' or '* text=auto eol=lf') makes checkouts byte-identical to blobs on every platform, or current mode hashes the git-normalised content (git hash-object --path / the clean filter). D-005 states the rule.
findings.actual: Candidate identity is not platform-independent in current mode; a Windows reviewer or CI runner cannot reproduce the frozen ID.

The test then adds a successful qa-verifier run for task T-DG0-LOAD (assignment docs/delivery/assignments/DG0/T-DG0-LOAD.md, started 11:00Z, before the 13:00Z freeze) and points findings.json F-DG0-201.verification.invocation_reference at it. validateGate() returns []. The run must start after the fix (at least after fix_revision was committed, or after the candidate the fix is in froze). It must have executed a review or verification assignment of this stage, for example the verifier's round-N assignment, whose record lists the finding in its <role>.verifications.json. A regression test must cover the pre-freeze LOAD-run case. Otherwise agents.md/D-016 must be corrected, but the gate condition 'independent verification' then remains unenforced.

findings.title: Reviewer-authored records and sidecars are not bound to the reviewer's run, and 'append-only' covers deletions only: editing them in place drops findings, flips FAIL verifications and FAIL verdicts
findings.reproduction: tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs:537-543 (checkReviewRounds) scans git history only with --diff-filter=D, so a committed file under reviews/<DGx>/ or runs/<DGx>/ may be MODIFIED in any later commit. Nothing binds the content of a review record (checkReview, rules.mjs:315-341), a findings sidecar (collectRaisedFindings, rules.mjs:345-370) or a verifications sidecar (collectVerifications, rules.mjs:454-481) to the run that supposedly wrote it: checkInvocation (rules.mjs:265-312) only proves that SOME successful run of that role exists. tools/agents/run-agent.sh:109-118 records no manifest of the files the agent wrote. Historical immutability (rules.mjs:586-626) starts only at the first commit where the gate record is APPROVED, and it pins whatever the files contained at that moment. Reproduced with GATE_TOOLS=/tmp/dg0-sec-r3 node --test docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/code-security/round-3/repro-r3.test.mjs (log 02-repro-r3-candidate.log): (a) test 4: round 1 raised High mandatory F-DG0-101, and the round-1 files were committed. A later commit rewrites round-1/code-security-reviewer.findings.json to {findings:[]}, sets the round-1 record's findings to [] and removes the entry from findings.json. validateGate current, validateGate historical (after approval) and validatePipeline all return []. (b) test 5: the reviewer's committed round-2 verifications sidecar says FAIL/OPEN. A later commit edits it to PASS/CLOSED_VERIFIED and mirrors findings.json. validateGate returns []. (c) test 6: a committed qa-verifier record with verdict FAIL and a FAIL check is edited to PASS. validateGate returns []. The real runs show a mechanical check is feasible: the transcripts contain the reviewer's Write/Bash tool calls. No file under reviews/DG0 or runs/DG0 has been modified or deleted in the real history so far (git log --diff-filter=D/M empty), so a stricter rule would not block DG0.
findings.expected: Once written by the reviewer's run, reviewer artefacts cannot be changed without the validator noticing. Minimum: (1) the history check rejects modifications as well as deletions (--diff-filter=DM, or first-committed blob == current blob) for every file under reviews/<DGx>/**, runs/<DGx>/** and the round's assignment, and it also compares the working tree with the first committed version. (2) The runner records the SHA-256 of every file the run created or changed (git status before/after) in meta.json, which is itself hash-bound. The validator requires every review record, findings sidecar and verifications sidecar to match the outputs of the run that its record cites. (3) The orchestrator commits the run's outputs together with its run directory immediately after the run, and D-016/D-018 describe the residual window. The error message 'review evidence is append-only' must be true.
findings.actual: The fixes for F-DG0-101/F-DG0-110 moved the source of truth from orchestrator-written findings.json to reviewer sidecars, but the sidecars and records can be edited by the same actor at the same cost (one JSON edit). An unresolved High finding can be removed, a reviewer's FAIL verification turned into a closure, or a FAIL review turned into PASS, and the gate, historical mode and pipeline still pass. D-018 states the evidence is append-only, but the implementation only forbids deletion.

findings.title: Working-tree candidate mode is read from the filesystem exec bit, so it disagrees with git where core.fileMode=false (Windows default); the result fails closed
findings.reproduction: tools/gates/lib/candidate.mjs:92 derives the mode of a working-tree file from st.mode & 0o111. Then candidate.mjs --stage DGx and validate.mjs --stage DGx (current mode) report a different ID from the frozen one, although git status is clean. repro-r3 test 9 simulates this on Linux: chmod -x plus core.fileMode=false gives an empty git status and a different working-tree candidate. findings.title: Write-once working-tree check is blind to skip-worktree/assume-unchanged index flags (local validation only)
findings.reproduction: tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs:593 (checkWriteOnce) detects uncommitted edits to committed evidence only through 'git status --porcelain'. The validator then reads the working-tree bytes (checkInvocation output binding, rules.mjs:310-318; collectVerifications). If a committed file is flagged with 'git update-index --skip-worktree' (or --assume-unchanged), git status stays empty while the file on disk differs. repro-r4.test.mjs test 13 ('BYPASS N2'): a committed round-2 FAIL/OPEN verification sidecar, its run's meta.json and findings.json are flagged skip-worktree. They are then edited on disk to PASS/CLOSED_VERIFIED, with meta.outputs re-pointed. 'git status --porcelain' is empty, and validateGate(repo,'DG0') returns [] (05-repro-r4-candidate.log). Impact is limited to a local working tree: CI checks out committed content, and committing the forgery shows up as an 'M' in history. But the release-auditor decides the gate by running validate.mjs locally.
findings.expected: The write-once check refuses to run (or reports an error) when any file under the write-once paths carries the skip-worktree or assume-unchanged flag. For example, 'git ls-files -v -- <paths>' must show no 'S' or lower-case tags. Alternatively, it compares working-tree bytes with the HEAD blob directly (hash each file and compare with 'git ls-tree HEAD').
findings.actual: A locally tampered working tree passes validate.mjs --stage DG0 with a clean git status. I would accept this as a Low observation if the orchestrator documents that the gate decision is re-validated from a clean checkout (CI), or adds the ls-files -v check.

findings.title: Run output binding records end-of-window bytes at any path a file tool was merely attempted on; 'exact bytes your run wrote with its file tools' is not what is checked
findings.reproduction: tools/agents/run-agent.sh:163-179 adds every Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit tool_use file_path from the transcript to written_by_tools, without looking at the matching tool_result, so hook-denied and failed calls count too. meta.outputs (run-agent.sh:160) is the post-snapshot hash taken when the run ends. The validator (rules.mjs:310-318) accepts a file when it equals meta.outputs and its path is in written_by_tools. So bytes produced by any other writer during the run window are bound as the reviewer's own: a Bash command, or a concurrent process such as the orchestrator's session. End-to-end with the real runner and a stub claude in a disposable clone (06-runner-e2e.log, FAKE_MODE=denied): the agent's Write of the review record is denied (tool_result is_error=true). Another writer puts 'B written by someone else' there during the window. meta.written_by_tools lists the record, meta.outputs holds sha256(B), and the runner auto-commits B as 'review evidence'. Real history shows the same gap in benign form (12-transcript-write-content.log): my own round-3 findings sidecar differs from the content of the run's Write call, because the same run later edited it with sed. The binding cannot tell the difference. The stream-json transcript does carry the full Write content and the tool_result status, so a stricter check is feasible.
findings.expected: Either (a) the runner counts only tool calls whose tool_result is not an error, and for Write records sha256(last successful Write content) per path. The validator, or the runner before auto-committing, requires the file to equal that content, and Edit/MultiEdit reconstruction is either done or those paths are flagged. Or (b) D-021 and agent-protocol.md ('the validator binds each of them to the exact bytes your run wrote with its file tools') are corrected to say what is actually bound: the bytes present at the end of the run window at paths the agent targeted with a file tool. The residual, overwrites by other writers during the window, is then disclosed next to the existing self-hashing residual.
findings.actual: The binding holds any end-of-window bytes at attempted paths. The documentation overstates it. The incremental risk is below the already disclosed residual (a fully fabricated run directory), so the severity is Low. It is not acceptable as an observation until the documentation matches the mechanism.

findings.title: Runner auto-commit passes reviewer-written paths as unquoted git pathspecs: glob characters commit unrelated files, and failures are masked by '|| true'
findings.reproduction: tools/agents/run-agent.sh:205-211 runs git add/commit with an unquoted $(cat "$OUT/../.commit-list-$RUN_ID"). Each written path is word-split by the shell and interpreted by git as a pathspec with glob magic. In a disposable clone with a stub claude (06-runner-e2e.log, FAKE_MODE=glob), the agent Writes a file literally named 'docs/delivery/reviews/DG0/round-9/x*'. An unrelated tracked file 'xy.md' in the same directory was modified by someone else during the window. The auto-commit 'run: <id> (review evidence ...)' contains 'A .../x*' and also 'M .../xy.md', which the agent never wrote. That turns another party's change into write-once 'review evidence' attributed to the run. By code inspection (not executed): a path containing whitespace is split into two pathspecs, 'git add' fails, and under set -e the runner then aborts before 'exit "$EXIT"' with the evidence uncommitted. The '|| true' on the commit (run-agent.sh:210) also hides every commit failure (hook, identity, lock), so the write-once window never starts, and neither meta.json nor the exit status records that.
findings.expected: Build the pathspec list safely: NUL-separated, 'git add --pathspec-from-file=- --pathspec-file-nul' with ':(literal)' magic or GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1. Commit exactly those paths. Treat 'nothing to commit' as the only tolerated non-zero result, and otherwise fail the runner with a distinct exit code and a message, so the orchestrator notices that the evidence was not committed.
findings.actual: Unrelated modified files can be swept into a reviewer's auto-commit, and commit failures are silent.

findings.reproduction: 1) git worktree add <tmp>/wt a059b55a7024f68cc7e33fedc8bd023d3b091336 (or git clone + checkout). 2) node tools/gates/candidate.mjs --stage DG0 prints sha256:c13a4f8e…3ff68 (matches the freeze). 3) Run tools/gates/prefreeze.sh DG0 (or only `python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/agents/tests -p 'test_*.py'`, which CI and prefreeze both run). Every check prints PASS, then 'FAIL  uncommitted candidate changes: M tools/agents/__pycache__/run_meta.cpython-311.pyc, M tools/agents/tests/__pycache__/test_run_meta.cpython-311.pyc', exit 1. 4) node tools/gates/candidate.mjs --stage DG0 now prints a different ID: sha256:e4008b07…7190e in the worktree, sha256:1d672b48…bbf33 in a fresh clone. Cause: commit d2630de (round-5 repair) added the two .pyc files. The frozen manifest lists them (c13a4f8e93cad95a.manifest.json lines 243 and 313), and the repo has no .gitignore. A CPython 3.11 .pyc header records the source mtime (here 1790608540 = 2026-09-28T15:15:40Z, the orchestrator's tree), and the code object embeds the absolute source path. Any other checkout has a different mtime and path, so importing run_meta.py recompiles and rewrites the cached files with checkout-specific bytes (13675 → 13740 bytes in the worktree).
findings.expected: The frozen candidate contains only source, with no machine-generated, checkout-specific build artefacts. Running every check the candidate ships (REQ-DLV-023: prefreeze.sh runs the Python unittest suite and then an uncommitted-changes check) passes on any fresh checkout of the candidate, and doesn't change the candidate's content or its recomputed candidate ID.
findings.actual: prefreeze.sh DG0 exits 1 on a fresh checkout of a059b55. It can pass only in the orchestrator's own working tree, where the source mtimes still match the committed caches. After the CI or prefreeze Python tests run, the working tree no longer hashes to the frozen candidate ID, and the drifted ID differs between checkouts. A reviewer who runs the required tests in the repository tree (rather than a disposable copy) would silently desynchronise the candidate. Fix: git rm --cached both .pyc files, add a .gitignore for __pycache__/ and *.pyc (or run the tests with PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 / -B in prefreeze and CI), and exclude such paths from the candidate manifest. Then re-freeze. I rate it Medium and mandatory: it is limited in scope and trivial to fix, but it breaks candidate reproducibility and makes a required DG0 check fail on the candidate.
